order: Add a .gitattributes file that pins line endings to LF for shell, JavaScript, and Markdown files, and mark install.sh executable in the repository. The goal is to stop a checkout from silently converting install.sh to CRLF line endings, which breaks its POSIX shebang line and makes the installer fail to run on Unix machines. Scope is two changes only: the new .gitattributes rules and the executable bit on install.sh — do not touch install.sh's contents or any other script. Cover the file extensions that matter for this installer path (.sh, .js, .md) without expanding the rule set to every text file in the tree, so the fix stays narrow and easy to reason about.
claims: Added .gitattributes with LF rules for sh/js/md files and set install.sh's executable bit; no other file content changed. This keeps a checkout on any platform from corrupting the installer's shebang line, since git now normalizes those extensions to LF regardless of the checking-out machine's default line-ending setting. Verified by inspecting the diff: five lines added to .gitattributes, a mode-only change on install.sh.
